subject: general
question: If m=a cos³β and n=b sin³β, then find the value of((m)/(a))⁽²⁾/⁽³⁾+((n)/(b))⁽²⁾/⁽³⁾
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Isolate the **trigonometric ratios**: m/a = cos³β and n/b = sin³β.

Raise both sides to the power 2/3: (m/a)²/³ = cos²β and (n/b)²/³ = sin²β.

Apply the **Pythagorean Identity**: sin²β + cos²β = 1.

**∴ The correct answer is 1.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

m = a cos³β

n = b sin³β

**Formula Used:**

sin²θ + cos²θ = 1

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/79e9b882f91e3526c263bca46fb0031f821c61fbeb311645b6055e924ae2cf01.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ m/a = cos³β

⇒ (m/a)¹/³ = cosβ

⇒ [(m/a)¹/³]² = cos²β

⇒ (m/a)²/³ = cos²β ---- (i)

⇒ n/b = sin³β

⇒ (n/b)¹/³ = sinβ

⇒ (n/b)²/³ = sin²β ---- (ii)

⇒ Adding (i) and (ii): (m/a)²/³ + (n/b)²/³ = cos²β + sin²β

⇒ Since sin²β + cos²β = 1, the result is 1.

**∴ The correct answer is 1.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Trigonometric Identities

Fundamental identities include sin²θ + cos²θ = 1, 1 + tan²θ = sec²θ, and 1 + cot²θ = cosec²θ.

Laws of Exponents

For any base x, (xa)b = xa×b. This property is used to eliminate cube powers by raising to 1/3 or 2/3.

Substitution Method

In competitive exams, you can substitute β = 0° or 90° to quickly find the value: if β = 0°, m/a = 1 and n/b = 0, result = 1 + 0 = 1.</p
